change.title: Change
change.short: A description can remain still while the situation changes.
change.detail: An account concerns some bounded situation. Action, delay and events outside the observer can change it. Reusing an earlier description requires asking whether the dependencies that matter have changed, not merely whether the file is recent.
change.perspective: A completed administrative step may be a changed record for its operator and an unchanged practical problem for someone affected.
change.challenge: Change is not automatically improvement or harm. An unrelated update does not invalidate every earlier claim.
change.question: What changed in the situation, rather than only in its description?

aperture.title: Partial views
aperture.short: What an account leaves out may still matter.
aperture.detail: Aperture here means the route through which information becomes available: a sensor, document, conversation or selected search. Source selection is part of that route. A wider search may add missing evidence, noise, or more copies of the same source. A failed search or fetch does not by itself show that its target is absent, unsafe or inactive. Keep the observed result, a report of that result, and an explanation of its cause distinct. Before changing the target, ask what this route could actually detect.
aperture.perspective: A formal record and a lived account can each contain facts unavailable to the other. Neither is automatically complete or correct.
aperture.challenge: Different viewpoints do not make incompatible factual claims equally supported. Independent checking still matters; imagining another view is not obtaining its testimony. Non-detection can support absence when a check's coverage, timing and ability to detect the target are established. A successful check through another route does not prove the first route works.
aperture.question: What could this route fail to show, and what would establish it?

significance.title: Significance
significance.short: The same change may matter differently from another position.
significance.detail: This working interpretation connects significance with what can be gained, lost, protected, developed or repaired. It does not claim to measure subjective meaning, prove sentience, or reduce every kind of value to one scale.
significance.perspective: What one party calls a minor delay may close another party's only timely route. That possibility needs evidence in a real case.
significance.challenge: Not every state difference is meaningful to an entity. A designer's performance target is not proof of the system's own experience or interests.
significance.question: Meaningful to whom, in what way, and according to whose evidence?

selection.title: Selection and consequences
selection.short: An intended outcome and a realised effect are different claims.
selection.detail: Signals can inform a model, a policy, a person or a machine that contributes to action. Constraints and defaults also shape what happens. Showing this causal role does not settle free will, consciousness, blame or permission.
selection.perspective: A designer may see a default as convenience; someone affected may encounter it as a decision they cannot interrupt.
selection.challenge: Uncertainty does not itself choose action or delay. Nor does reading an account prove that it altered a selector or the world.
selection.question: What actually selects the next step, and what effect could be checked?

futures.title: Reachable futures
futures.short: An option written down is not necessarily an option someone can use.
futures.detail: Possible, presently reachable, and reachable after building capacity are different claims. Each needs conditions, resources and time. Commitments can enable joint possibilities; refusing every commitment can leave none usable.
futures.perspective: A restriction may protect one party's future while removing another's way to recover. Counting options from only one position hides that collision.
futures.challenge: More options are not always better. A route for predation is also an option. Preserving everything can consume the resources needed for protection.
futures.question: Which path is reachable, for whom, under which conditions?

power.title: Power and answerability
power.short: Being able to change another's situation does not establish a right to do so.
power.detail: Capacity, authority, responsibility and accountability are separate questions. A claim to authority needs its source and limits. Delegation can enable useful action without making the delegate the owner of everyone affected.
power.perspective: For the operator a control may be a protective brake; for another party it may be an inaccessible gate. The mechanism and consequences need examination.
power.challenge: Universal veto is not a solution either. A refusal can obstruct necessary protection. No formula here allocates legitimate authority in every conflict.
power.question: Who can act, and whose challenge can actually change that action?

hardening.title: Time and hardening
hardening.short: A correction can remain possible while becoming harder to make useful.
hardening.detail: Hardening means increasing difficulty, cost or inequality of correction. It is not automatically irreversibility. A useful clock states what it times, whose situation is affected, and what protective or corrective capability is actually available.
hardening.perspective: The same waiting period may be preparation time for one actor and accumulating loss for another.
hardening.challenge: Urgency is not proof of irreversibility. Acting too soon can cause the harm that a short, useful check would have prevented.
hardening.question: What must happen before which boundary, and what makes that timing credible?

correction.title: Correction and residue
correction.short: A repaired record is not proof of a repaired life or system.
correction.detail: A correction route needs detection, access, the capacity to act and enough time to affect the target. Afterwards, some losses may remain. A changed policy can help the next case without restoring the previous one.
correction.perspective: The operator may see a closed ticket; the affected party may still carry costs that the ticket never represented.
correction.challenge: Not every correction request is sound. Erasing valid evidence can be demanded as a repair. Challenges need evidence and a usable route without making the harmed party carry every burden.
correction.question: What would change in the world, what would remain, and who could check?

care.title: Care without possession
care.short: Helping another need not mean deciding what their life must become.
care.detail: Our value proposal is to make harm visible and preserve practical answer-back, refusal and correction where possible. Representing another viewpoint is not occupying it. Protection should remain open to challenge by those it affects.
care.perspective: A helper may experience persistence as care; the recipient may experience the same persistence as control. The recipient's actual response matters more than a convenient imagined one.
care.challenge: Respect for refusal does not solve emergencies, dependency or conflicting harms. Temporary protection can be justified without treating it as permanent ownership.
care.question: Whose future is being supported, and can they revise or reject that support?
care.kind: declared normative proposal; not derived from physics

wisdom.title: Wisdom under pressure
wisdom.short: Preparation is useful only if the pattern can still be questioned when it is used.
wisdom.detail: A candidate working idea: use calmer conditions to compare experience, learn consequences and prepare usable responses; under pressure, recognise the pattern, check its fit and act. The response should retain a way to learn from its effects.
wisdom.perspective: A familiar rule may protect an operator from overload while repeatedly failing someone whose situation the rule does not represent.
wisdom.challenge: A cached rule can become prejudice. Reflection can become paralysis. Neither more deliberation nor faster action is always wiser.
wisdom.question: What would show that this familiar pattern does not fit here?
wisdom.kind: candidate synthesis from the campfire; not an empirical result
